intro.text: A Variable Periodic Schedule consent authorises a TPP to initiate one payment per period at a variable amount up to a defined ceiling. The user authorises once — approving a maximum per-payment amount and the recurring period — and the TPP submits one payment per period without requiring re-authorisation each time.
Common use cases include variable monthly utility bills, periodic service charges, and TPP-managed savings sweeps where the amount differs each period but must stay within a pre-approved cap.

sections.heading: What you need before initiating a Variable Periodic Schedule payment

blocks.text: Before initiating a Variable Periodic Schedule payment, ensure the following requirements are met:

items: Registered Application — the application must be created within the Trust Framework and assigned the BSIP role as defined in Roles.
Valid Transport Certificate — an active transport certificate must be issued and registered in the Trust Framework to establish secure mTLS communication.
Valid Signing Certificate — an active signing certificate must be issued and registered in the Trust Framework. This certificate is used to sign request objects and client assertions.
Registration with the relevant API Hub (Authorisation Server) — the application must be registered with the API Hub (Server) of the LFI with which you intend to initiate payments.

Understanding of the FAPI Security Profile and Tokens & Assertions — you should understand how request object signing, client authentication, and access token validation underpin secure API interactions.

Understanding of Message Encryption — PII (creditor name and account details) must be encrypted as a JWE before being embedded in the consent. You will need the LFI's public encryption key from their JWKS.

sections.heading: Sign and encrypt the consent PII

blocks.text: With the encrypted PII ready, construct the authorization_details of type urn:openfinanceuae:service-initiation-consent:v2.2. Set PeriodicSchedule.Type to "VariablePeriodicSchedule". Unlike Fixed Periodic Schedule, the amount is not fixed at consent time — each POST /payments call specifies its own amount, subject to the MaximumIndividualAmount ceiling. Only one payment may be submitted per period.

There is no Controls block — the period itself acts as the limiting boundary, and MaximumIndividualAmount caps each payment's value.

rows: The period length: Day, Week, Month, or Year

blocks.text: Only one payment may be submitted per period. The API Hub will reject a second POST /payments call within the same period, even if the amount is within the ceiling.

sections.heading: Submit one payment per period, up to the ceiling
sections.category: Initiating Payments on a Periodic Schedule · Step 9 — POST /payments

blocks.text: Include x-fapi-interaction-id and x-idempotency-key. If the customer is present at this point in the flow, also send x-fapi-customer-ip-address, x-customer-user-agent and x-fapi-auth-date if the customer has been authenticated. See Request Headers.

Submit one payment per period under this consent. Each call specifies the actual amount for that period — it must be ≤ MaximumIndividualAmount. The API Hub will reject a second payment submitted within the same period and any payment that exceeds the ceiling.

Unlike Single Instant Payment, multi-payment consents do not require PaymentPurposeCode, DebtorReference, CreditorReference, or OpenFinanceBilling to match the consent exactly. Only ConsentId must match the authorized consent. Instruction.Amount must be within the parameters the consent allows for this payment type.

The consent permits exactly one POST /payments call per period. Submitting a second payment within the same period will be rejected, regardless of the amount. Plan your payment schedule so that one payment is submitted after each period boundary.

The API Hub will reject a payment if Instruction.Amount exceeds MaximumIndividualAmount, if a payment has already been submitted in the current period, or if any lifetime cumulative cap has been reached.

sections.heading: Use the refresh_token to keep the session alive

blocks.text: After each successful payment, the consent remains in the Authorized state until the next period begins (unless lifetime cumulative caps are reached or the consent expires). You do not need to re-initiate the authorization flow.
